findings.note: Item 4 answer states a list of legal roles and a legal conclusion with no cited claim and no ledger support: 'Only someone with legal authority to sign. That might be the owner, a trustee, an executor or administrator, or several heirs who agree. Living in the house alone does not give you that authority.' The ledger has no authority or probate claim (clm:1-7 cover only H&S 17920.3 and Civ. Code 1102/1102.6). Remove the list of roles and the sentence 'Living in the house alone does not give you that authority', or state only that the person who signs must have legal authority and the seller should confirm who that is with an attorney or title company.

Item 3 says 'The statute does not mention hoarding.' This is a statement about the text of H&S 17920.3 that no ledger claim (clm:1-4) records; it appears only as a brief open item. Ask for a ledger claim or stored passage backing it, or soften to 'The listed conditions do not name hoarding.' Not blocking because the brief carries it deliberately.

required_actions: Item 4 (Who can sell the house): remove the role list and the 'Living in the house alone does not give you that authority' conclusion, or limit to 'the person signing must have legal authority; confirm who with an attorney or title company'.
